entries.title: Acts 18:1
segments: After this Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

entries.title: Acts 18:2
segments: Here he found a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife, Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome.

entries.title: Acts 18:3
segments: Paul came to them, and because he was of the same trade with them, he lodged with them, and worked with them--for by trade they were tentmakers.

entries.title: Acts 18:4
segments: Every Sabbath he used to preach in the synagogue, and tried to persuade both Jews and Greeks.

entries.title: Acts 18:5
segments: And when Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul was engrossed in his message, earnestly testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Messiah.

entries.title: Acts 18:6
segments: But as they opposed him and abused him, he shook out his garments in protest, and said: "Your blood be upon your own hands. I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."

entries.title: Acts 18:7
segments: So he left the place, and went into the house of a man named Titus Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house adjoined the synagogue.

entries.title: Acts 18:8
segments: And Crispus, the warden of the synagogue, believed on the Lord, with all his household; and many of the Corinthians from time to time listened, believed, and were baptized.

entries.title: Acts 18:9
segments: And the Lord said to Paul in a vision, by night: "Have no fear; go on speaking, and do not keep silent;

entries.title: Acts 18:10
segments: "for I am with you, and no one shall set upon you to injure you; for I have very many people in this city."

entries.title: Acts 18:11
segments: So he lived there a year and six months and continued to teach them the word of God.

entries.title: Acts 18:12
segments: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose against Paul, and brought him before the tribunal.

entries.title: Acts 18:13
segments: "This fellow," they said, "is persuading men to offer unlawful worship to God."

entries.title: Acts 18:14
segments: Paul was about to open his mouth, when Gallio said to the Jews: "If it had been some misdemeanor or wicked villainy, it would have been within reason for me to listen to you Jews;

entries.title: Acts 18:15
segments: but as these are merely questions about words and names and your own law, you yourselves must see to it. I am not willing to be a judge of these matters."

entries.title: Acts 18:16
segments: And he drove them from the tribunal.

entries.title: Acts 18:17
segments: Then they all laid hold of Sosthenes, the warden of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the tribunal; but Gallio took no notice.

entries.title: Acts 18:18
segments: And Paul after remaining in Corinth some time longer, took leave of the brothers, and sailed away to Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila. As Paul was under a vow, he had his head shaved at Cenchrea.

entries.title: Acts 18:19
segments: When they came to Ephesus he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

entries.title: Acts 18:20
segments: When they begged him to stay longer, he would not consent,

entries.title: Acts 18:21
segments: but said, as he took leave of them, "I will return again to you, if God will."

entries.title: Acts 18:22
segments: Then, setting sail from Ephesus, he landed at Caesarea; he went up to Jerusalem and saluted the church, and came down to Antioch.

entries.title: Acts 18:23
segments: After spending some time there, he set out and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, and strengthened all the disciples.

entries.title: Acts 18:24
segments: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, a learned man and mighty in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus.

entries.title: Acts 18:25
segments: He had been instructed in the ways of the Lord, and being full of zeal, he used to speak and to teach accurately the facts about Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.

entries.title: Acts 18:26
segments: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue; and when Priscilla and Aquila heard him they took him home and explained to him more accurately the way of God.

entries.title: Acts 18:27
segments: When he wished to cross over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him, and wrote to the disciples in Corinth to receive him. On his arrival he mightily helped those who through grace had believed,

entries.title: Acts 18:28
segments: for he powerfully refuted the Jews in public argument, proving to them from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Messiah.
